hints: Focus on what percentage by mass really means, the total mass of nitrogen atoms divided by the total mass of one formula unit.
Count the nitrogen atoms first. Each fertiliser here actually contains two N atoms, so the winner will be the one with the smallest Mr.
Work out Mr for each compound and compare 28 divided by Mr to see which fraction gives the largest percentage.
walkthrough:
**Recall the percentage by mass rule**

Great start, this is a comparison question. For any compound, the % of an element is the mass of that element in one mole divided by the molar mass.

$$\% \text{ N} = \frac{\text{mass of N in formula}}{M_r \text{ of compound}} \times 100$$

**Count nitrogen in each fertiliser**

Look carefully, each formula contains 2 nitrogen atoms. So each has $2 \times 14.0 = 28.0$ g of N per mole.

$\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$: 2 N, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$: 2 N, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{HPO}_4$: 2 N, $\text{CO}(\text{NH}_2)_2$: 2 N

**Compare and pick the greatest %**

Since the top of the fraction is always 28, the smallest bottom gives the biggest percentage. Urea has by far the smallest Mr.

$$\% \text{ N in urea} = \frac{28}{60} \times 100 = 46.7\%$$
Compared to $35.0\%$ for ammonium nitrate and about $21.2\%$ for the other two, urea is clearly the winner.

options.A: Ammonium nitrate has $M_r = 80$ and %N = 28/80 x 100 = 35.0%. This is high, which is why it is a popular fertiliser, but it is still lower than urea because its Mr is larger.
options.B: Ammonium sulfate has $M_r = 132$ and %N = 28/132 x 100 = 21.2%. The heavy sulfate group, $\text{SO}_4$, dilutes the nitrogen content a lot.
options.C: Diammonium hydrogen phosphate also has $M_r = 132$ and %N = 28/132 x 100 = 21.2%. The heavy phosphate group makes this the joint lowest with ammonium sulfate.
options.D: Urea, $\text{CO}(\text{NH}_2)_2$, has the smallest $M_r = 60$ with the same 28 g of N, giving %N = 28/60 x 100 = 46.7%. This is the greatest percentage of nitrogen by mass.
